Added 2026-08-27, per Josh ('labels on the Xaxes ... do not appear to be the real dates'): with theme_bw()'s default (~5.5pt) spacing, the rightmost x-axis label of one panel (centered exactly at date.end, per $xaxe.interval) visually overlaps the leftmost label of the next panel (centered at date.start), making both look garbled even though each date is individually correct. First tried raising this to 40pt to add clearance, but since the overall saved figure width is fixed ($plot.width + $ggsave.width.pad, not something that grows with panel-gap width), widening the gaps shrank every panel's own width instead - which then cut off a long facet title ('Eastern small-footed myotis'). Reverted to theme_bw()'s own default ('5.5', a plain value revert - this is a no-op vs. not having the setting at all, kept so it stays available to override later) per Josh's explicit correction ('revert back to the previous plot dimensions'); the label-collision problem is now solved via $axis.text.size instead (see that row below), which needs less horizontal room rather than more.

Facet strip text (e.g. species panel titles) is not independently configurable in the code as written; it always renders at ggplot2's own fixed size (rel(0.8) of theme_bw()'s base_size 11 = 8.8pt).

Reduced from 8 to 6 on 2026-08-27, per Josh ('reduce the size of the labels on the x and y axis until there is no overlap'): with $panel.spacing.x reverted to its original '5.5' (see that row above), smaller tick-label text needs less horizontal room, so the two-line X-axis date labels clear each other at every panel boundary without needing extra panel spacing. Verified by pixel-cropping the rendered panel boundary at several candidate sizes: 8/7/6.5 still show visible character overlap between adjacent panels' date labels; 6 is the first size with a clean, non-overlapping gap.
